questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Terminal Speed of Rail-Sliding Rods in Gravity
questions.category: Electromagnetic Induction & AC :: Multi-Concept Physical Modeling (Type 2)
questions.question: A conducting rod of length $\ell$, mass $m$, and resistance $R$ in [Electromagnetic Induction & AC] slides down frictionless vertical rails in a horizontal uniform magnetic field $B$. What is its terminal velocity under gravity?
questions.solution: Induced EMF is $\mathcal{E} = B \ell v$, current is $I = \frac{B \ell v}{R}$, and upward magnetic Lorentz force is $F_B = I \ell B = \frac{B^2 \ell^2 v}{R}$. At terminal velocity, $F_B = mg \implies v_t = \frac{mgR}{B^2 \ell^2}$.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Electromagnetic Induction & AC.
tags: Terminal Speed of Rail-Sliding Rods in Gravity

questions.topic: Terminal Speed of Rail-Sliding Rods in Gravity
questions.category: Electromagnetic Induction & AC :: Numerical Derivation
questions.question: One mole of ideal gas undergoes a polytropic expansion $P V^2 = C$ in [Electromagnetic Induction & AC] from volume $V_0 = 1\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $P_0 = 10^5\text{ Pa}$ to $V_1 = 2\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the magnitude of work done by the gas in $\text{kJ}$ rounded to nearest integer.
questions.solution: Work done in polytropic process with $n=2$: $W = \frac{P_0 V_0 - P_1 V_1}{n - 1} = P_0 V_0 \left(1 - \frac{V_0}{V_1}\right) = 10^5 \times 1 \times (1 - 0.5) = 5 \times 10^4\text{ J} = 50\text{ kJ}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Electromagnetic Induction & AC.
tags: Terminal Speed of Rail-Sliding Rods in Gravity
